PDM and LSTM benchmark protocol

Source: benchmark-protocol.md

Draft for agreement. Version 0.1, 2026-10-31.

This protocol fixes how PDM and the LSTM models are compared before anyone sees a test result. Its purpose is simple: if the comparison is challenged, the answer is this document, dated and agreed in advance. Items in square brackets are open decisions. They must be closed, and the protocol versioned, before the test period is scored.

1. Principle

Both models get the same data, the same periods and a stated, comparable search effort. Both are scored by the same code on the same masked observations. A basin enters or leaves the comparison for data reasons decided in advance, never because of its result.

The comparison is in simulation mode. Neither model sees observed flow at run time: PDM’s updating and state correction are off, and the LSTM takes no lagged discharge input. Forecast skill with assimilation is a different question and needs its own protocol.

2. Basins

  • The basin list is fixed in an appendix before calibration starts: [60 basins, list to follow].
  • Selection criteria are recorded with the list: [record length, data completeness, no significant regulation or abstraction, catchment area range].
  • A basin is excluded only for data reasons found before scoring: for example, a gauge record with more than [10] per cent missing in the test period, or forcing that cannot be infilled. The reason is recorded. No basin is removed after test results exist.

3. Data

  • Time step: 15 minutes, UTC, for both models.
  • Forcing: both models receive the same rainfall and PET series, in mm per interval, from the same source and processing chain. Gaps are infilled once, by one method, before either model sees the data.
  • Static inputs: the LSTM may also use catchment attributes; PDM uses only catchment area. This is a legitimate difference between a regional and a per-basin model, not a fairness breach, but it is stated in every report: [list of LSTM static attributes].
  • Observed flow: in m3/s, mean flow over each interval, matching PDM’s q_m3s. Missing observations stay missing. They are never infilled for scoring.

4. Periods

Periods are chronological and do not overlap. The same dates apply to every basin and both models.

Period Dates PDM use LSTM use
Warm-up [1 year before calibration] Simulated, not scored Sequence look-back
Calibration or training [YYYY to YYYY] Parameter estimation Weight training
Tuning [YYYY to YYYY] Not used Early stopping and hyperparameters
Test [YYYY to YYYY], about the final [7] years Scored once Scored once

The test period is scored once, after both models are frozen. Any rerun after test results are known is reported as such, with the reason.

PDM does not need a tuning period. It may be calibrated on calibration and tuning combined, so that it sees the same span of data as the LSTM: [decide; recommended: yes].

5. PDM configuration

  • Package: pdmS7 at a recorded commit, compiled engine, adaptive groundwater solver.
  • Structure: Pareto capacity, standard recharge, two-store surface cascade, cubic groundwater, no snow. The same structure for every basin.
  • Parameters and bounds: [list in an appendix]. Bounds are set from catchment knowledge before calibration and are not changed after test results exist.
  • Objective: 1 minus NSE on q_m3s, warm-up excluded.
  • Search effort: [k] L-BFGS-B starts per basin, with k set by the pilot (inst/examples/pilot_calibration.R); maximum 200 iterations per start; seed 1000 plus the basin’s index in the appendix list.
  • Diagnostics recorded per basin: start_results in full, with every start’s objective, convergence code, evaluation count and fitted parameters; parameters within 1 per cent of a bound; wall time.

6. LSTM configuration

  • Architecture and inputs: [specify]. Fixed before training.
  • Loss: [NSE-based loss, per-basin normalised, or as agreed]. State it if it differs from PDM’s objective.
  • Hyperparameter search: on the tuning period only, with the search space and number of trials recorded.
  • Search effort: [n] training seeds. The reported model is [the ensemble mean, or the median seed]; the spread across seeds is reported alongside.
  • Output handling: negative predicted flows are set to zero before scoring, and the number of intervals affected is reported.

7. Search effort and compute

The two models search in different ways, so effort cannot be equalised exactly. It is reported instead: PDM starts and objective evaluations against LSTM seeds, trials and epochs, with core-hours or GPU-hours for each. A reader can then judge whether either model was under-resourced.

8. Metrics

All metrics are computed on the test period by pdm_objectives() from pdmS7, for both models, using the same observation mask. One scoring function removes one class of argument. The function returns losses; the report converts them where noted.

Metric pdm_objectives() name Reported as What it shows
NSE nse_loss 1 minus the loss Overall fit, dominated by high flows
KGE kge_loss 1 minus the loss Correlation, variability and bias together
RMSE of log flows log_rmse (offset [0.01] m3/s) As returned Low-flow behaviour
Volume bias abs_bias As returned Water balance
Peak magnitude error peak_relative_error As returned Size of the largest flow in the test period

KGE’s three terms (correlation, variability ratio, bias ratio) explain where a fit fails, but pdm_objectives() does not return them separately. If wanted, they are computed from the same masked series by one shared function, written and agreed before scoring: [decide].

Peak timing is not assessed: the package has no timing metric, and adding one is deferred. Event-based peak analysis, if wanted, needs an agreed event definition and belongs in a protocol revision.

9. Comparison and reporting

  • Per basin: every metric for both models in one table, including basins where PDM wins.
  • Across basins: median and interquartile range of each metric, and cumulative distribution plots.
  • Paired comparison: per-basin differences, the count of basins each model wins on each metric, and a Wilcoxon signed-rank test as a descriptive summary, not a verdict.
  • Diagnostics: PDM basins with parameters on a bound or no converged start are flagged, not dropped. Results are reported with and without them.
  • Stratification: results by [catchment area, baseflow index, flashiness] if agreed in advance. Strata chosen after seeing results are labelled as exploratory.

10. Reproducibility

Recorded with the results: package commit, R version, operating system, seeds, the frozen configuration for each basin, the LSTM code version and weights, and the scored series. The outputs are archived with this protocol.

11. Changes to this protocol

Each change is versioned with its date and reason. A change made after any test result is known is reported in the results, with the comparison under the original protocol where possible.

Open decisions

Item Section Owner Recommendation
Basin list and selection criteria 2 [ ] Fix before the pilot finishes
Missing-data exclusion threshold 2 [ ] 10 per cent in the test period
LSTM static attributes 3 [ ] List explicitly
Period dates 4 [ ] Final 7 years as test
PDM on calibration plus tuning 4 [ ] Yes, to match the data span
PDM bounds 5 [ ] From catchment knowledge, before calibration
PDM starts, k 5 [ ] From the pilot
LSTM loss, seeds, ensemble rule 6 [ ] Ensemble mean, spread reported
Log offset 8 [ ] 0.01 m3/s, or 1 per cent of mean flow
KGE terms reported separately 8 [ ] Yes, from one shared function
Strata 9 [ ] Agree before scoring
